And they will merit the coming of the redeemer (the Messiah) through fulfilling all worldly actions in accordance with His will,and by elevating all the sparks of the Shechinah, especially those embedded in speech — in prayer and Torah — when those are done truly, from the heart.  Then, the world of speech will be elevated, and all fallen letters and words will rise.  And their prayers will be accepted, because they are genuine and from a full heart.  And all the spiritual attributes that were previously clothed in material forms, as explained earlier, will be elevated back to their source, when they are used in service of the Creator.  And abundant blessing will flow into the world.  But until they repent, as long as they damage those attributes, and use them for sin and transgression, they cause lengthening of the exile, and bring upon themselves judgment and suffering, God forbid.  And this is the intent of the verse, according to our path of interpretation.

"And I pleaded with the Lord at that time, saying" – interpretation: by means of what I see that is written by Your prophet there, saying, "Behold, a man sends his wife, etc." – for there it is explained that in the end, I must return to You, because (Isaiah 50:1), "Where is the bill of divorce of your mother?" – that the Blessed Creator betrothed us forever, as it is written (Hosea 2:21), "And I will betroth you to Me forever."  And also from there I see that even though I have committed harlotry with many lovers, nonetheless You said, "Return to Me." On account of this, I was comforted in my heart and returned to You, and I pleaded by means of the reading of that portion which begins, "Behold, a man sends, etc."  "Adonai Hashem" – interpretation: may it be Your will that the aspect of Adonai pray within Havayah (the Tetragrammaton), that there be an elevation of the sparks, portions of the Shechinah, through our actions and our speech, and that there no longer be judgments in the world that come from the aspect of Adonai, "the law of the kingdom is law," as is known.  And all of this is due to the lack of unification and the elevation of the sparks of the Shechinah.  "For You have begun" – interpretation: the language of sickness and judgments – that until now, the sickness of judgments and troubles upon Israel, may the Merciful One save us, is in order "to show Your servant Your greatness and Your strong hand."  Interpretation: "Your greatness" is the "Great Hand," which is a reference to the attribute of love and kindness, and "Your strong hand" is a reference to the attribute of awe and strength – that all the troubles that You began with Israel are because they did not see and turned a blind eye to the attributes: the Great Hand, which is love, and the attribute of awe – the Strong Hand – that were clothed in the primary conduct of the world, which are silver and gold. And they did not look to the inner meaning, the intent of the Creator, blessed be He.  And furthermore, they angered Him with those very attributes, may He be blessed. Therefore, it came upon them through the blemish of the attributes clothed there as the sickness of troubles and the long, bitter exile – in order that they pay attention to see the inner essence of love and awe.  And this is what it says: "two hands for the Mishkan" – that in order to be in the aspect of a Mishkan (dwelling) for the Creator, blessed be He, as it says (Exodus 25:8), "And I will dwell among them," one must acquire the two hands in completeness.  And this is: "You have begun them with the sickness of troubles and judgments in order to show Your servant Your greatness" – this is the attribute of love – "and Your strong hand" – this is the attribute of awe – so that they may see them in their inner aspect, and not in the externality.  And now, after repentance, when they have given their hearts to return to You and to see the truth – then Adonai will be included to become Havayah, and there will no longer be the sickness of judgments, since they have come to Your intent.  And we will merit once again to see the miracles and wonders that You will do with us in our redemption, until all the nations will say: "Who is a God in heaven and earth who can do according to Your deeds and according to Your might?" And it will be fulfilled in us (Micah 7:15), "As in the days of your coming out of Egypt, I will show you wonders." Amen, forever and ever, Selah.  Blessed is the Lord forever, Amen and Amen.

“And I pleaded with the Lord at that time… You have begun… Your greatness and Your strong hand…” – and Rashi explains: Even though the righteous could rely on their good deeds, they ask only for an undeserved gift, for the word chanun (gracious) always implies a free gift. To understand this: why has it truly become established in the minds of the righteous that, despite their deeds, they should request only a free gift?

Let us first introduce the verse (Deuteronomy 8:17–18): "You may say in your heart, ‘My strength and the power of my hand made me this wealth,’ but you shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you the strength to make wealth." Onkelos translates this as: "For He gives you counsel to acquire possessions." According to the Targum’s interpretation, every Jew must believe that in all aspects of life — whether material, in earning a livelihood and worldly matters, or spiritual, in serving the Blessed God — the counsel and understanding that comes to his mind before taking action is sent from the heights of holiness, guiding him on the path he should take to succeed and profit in that transaction or endeavor. This is because, at that time, it is the will of the Blessed God that things should go that way. Conversely, Heaven forbid, if it is God’s will to bring him to a loss, He places in his heart the thought and desire to act in a certain way that will lead to that loss — since, due to some spiritual blockage or unworthiness, he cannot receive the goodness and compassion of the Blessed Creator. For even though "from the mouth of the Most High evil does not come forth" (Lamentations 3:38), nevertheless, when a person — who is literally a portion of God — becomes disconnected from his divine root, which is the source of all things where only pure mercy flows, then that disconnection causes him to fall into lower worlds where judgment prevails. There, in the Heavenly Court, strict justice is applied according to his deeds, out of honor for the Divine. About this, King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 17:2): "Let my judgment come forth from before You" — meaning, since "Your eyes behold uprightness," and You act only with absolute mercy toward people, therefore my request is: may my judgment come directly from before You — so that You assist me and prevent me from becoming detached from You, Heaven forbid, and falling into the place of judgment, to be judged in the Heavenly Court. Rather, I should always remain connected above — ever higher — to the Source of all, where there are no judgments at all, only pure mercy.

And for your understanding, the matter is known that there are twenty-eight times that King Solomon, peace be upon him, considered in Ecclesiastes chapter 3 — fourteen times for good and fourteen times for bad — upon which all the events of the world depend, both for good and for betterment; and these represent the secret of the left and right hands, called thus for kindnesses and severities as is well known. Therefore, every servant of the Lord must include the left within the right, so that the severities may be encompassed by kindnesses — fourteen bad times within the good times — and all becomes good by the sweetening of the severities. Moreover, all this is due to the fact that in the creation of man there is the aspect of left and right, which is the good inclination and the evil inclination, as is well known. The dwelling of the good inclination is in the heart of man in the right chamber, while the dwelling of the evil inclination is in the left chamber; and a person’s tendency is to direct himself to the left side, thereby bringing himself into the fourteen bad times which are the Lord of hosts, the severities and judgments. Hence, one must overcome and incline himself, along with all the traits engraved within him from the superior traits, to guide them to the right, so that all his actions will be for the sake of Heaven and to fulfill “In all your ways know Him” (Proverbs 3:6), as mentioned elsewhere, and also “And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart” — that is, with the two inclinations, the good inclination and the evil inclination — to subdue the servant under his master, so that no trait among the traits falls outside the service of His blessed name. For the wise will understand and set his heart, recognizing that the whole earth is full of His glory, and there is no vacant place at all, even in physical matters and business dealings; all is His service and refinement of holiness, from the place of breaking, which is the language of dealings upwards to the place of the root from which the matter fell; that which comes to his hand belongs to the root of his soul that uplifts him upwards, and not through it is he drawn, God forbid, after the evil which is the garment of holiness that clothed it in its fall and caused it, God forbid, to fall even further downward. Only “In all your ways know Him” — which is the language of connection, to join and bind the vitality in every thing with the vitality imparted to it for the life of lives — and he should look at the vitality in every thing and not at the material that clothes that thing. And all this is due to the fact that even when it is within him, he is not drawn after the material, only that the overcoming vitality is always with him over the material, and therefore he sees thus in all things that the main thing is vitality; and through this it is likewise done above, with the lower arousal being the upper arousal, and all the severities and judgments are sweetened by kindnesses, so that all becomes complete kindness through his cleaving to the root of all; He pours kindness into all things and into the whole world and its fullness, and the left is included in the right, and all twenty-eight times become equal for good through the sweetening mentioned above, which is the power of the Lord. Regarding this, Moses our teacher prayed and said, “And now, please let the power of the Lord be great,” for when Israel sinned with the spies and fell from faith, which is the principal foundation, as it is said (Habakkuk 2:4), “The righteous shall live by his faith,” they fell into the place of judgments and death, and the twenty-eight times separated, and the severities were not encompassed by kindness, and through this judgments came upon them as is known. Therefore, Moses prayed and said, “And now, please let the power of the Lord be great,” so that the twenty-eight times may grow in the Lord, who is mercy and kindness, that they be included together, and the power will increase, as is known that the main power is in the right hand, “And from my flesh I shall see God” (Job 19:26). Conversely, when they are not included in the right, but separated, it is said, “And they went without strength before the pursuer.” This is what is written, “In your midst holiness, and I will not enter the city” — the Holy One, blessed be He, swore that He would not enter the upper Jerusalem until He entered the lower Jerusalem, which is the intention above. For it is known that Jerusalem is the middle point of the world, for in it is the foundation stone from which the world was established, and the heart is called by the name Jerusalem because it is the middle point from the main body to the feet, and the heart is the dwelling of the divine portion imparted within man from above, as it is written (Exodus 25:8), “And I will dwell among them.” The Creator, blessed be He, does not place His presence in the heart of man until his service is as it is said, “with all your heart” — with the two inclinations — so that the evil inclination, which is the left chamber, will be included and sweetened by the right for the service of the Blessed One, so that his whole heart with the two chambers will be entirely good. Through this, his heart becomes the dwelling place of the Lord, as it is said, “The temple of the Lord they are indeed.” Whereas if the left chamber is not sweetened, God says, “I and he cannot dwell together,” and a person cannot walk with a snake in one basket. And this is “In your midst holiness,” because the Holy One, blessed be He, places His presence in your midst; therefore, see that no foreign god be in your heart, God forbid. He will not enter the upper Jerusalem until He enters the lower Jerusalem, which is the heart, the dwelling of His presence; then He will enter the upper Jerusalem, for in the lower arousal, which is the unification and sweetening of severities in the heart, it will be so above, that His mercy will be drawn into the lower worlds and the severities will be included in His Infinite Light, blessed be He, from which mercy comes. All the above only comes through knowledge, that one should have the knowledge that all the power one has, both to act and to speak — any speech — is all by the vitality given to him from above, without which he cannot move any limb from his limbs; and the words are poured to him from above from the World of Speech, and are concentrated in the mouth of man, as it is said, “O Lord, open my lips” (Psalms 51:17), and as the Arizal, of blessed memory, said, the intention is that the dominion which is the World of Speech speaks inside the mouth of man. As is explained at length elsewhere, this is the aspect of His presence which dwells within us, as it is said, “Wherever the Shechinah went out with them,” that the power of the higher speech is always with them in all their exile, and all this is their consolation in the bitterness of this exile. For immediately when a person wills, he can draw near himself by good knowledge and cleaving to the Blessed Creator through the speech fixed in his mouth, when he unites his heart with the speech so that there be no separation within his heart, as mentioned, that the two inclinations, the good and the evil, be arranged so that the heart turns away from evil, and the sweetening of severities by kindness be as above. Through this, he can nullify all bad decrees and judgments, God forbid, that come upon the world. As it is said, “A righteous person rules through the fear of God, who rules over me? The righteous in Israel,” specifically by the infusion of the Creator, blessed be He, within him, that the severities are sweetened; accordingly his speech is rectified, which brings in the Infinite Light, blessed be He, into the words, and it is made above likewise, so that the judgments in the World of Judgment, which is “Adonai Dina D’Malchuta Dina,” the law of the kingdom, are sweetened, and the World of Speech is unified. As is known, the Creator, blessed be He, contracts Himself from Above to Below through ten intellects and supernal lights down to the World of Speech, which is dominion that governs His world with kindness, so that the children of the world are not separated in their speech and all their deeds, from which blessed be He spreads mercy from Above to Below in a chain from world to world through ten intellects, as said about the World of Speech which is “Adonai Eretz,” and governance is by mercy. All this is through the lower arousal of faith and knowledge, for “The mouth of the Lord has spoken,” as said, one can receive mercy and it is done and drawn through this. As is known, the world was created by ten utterances, and “Bereishit” is also an utterance, which is why no “He said” is mentioned in it, because it is a supernal world called “Ayin,” where there is no aspect of speech until the chain from world to world reaches the tenth utterance, which is “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made” (Psalms 33:6), through which world His kingdom is revealed and grasped by the lower world, as is explained elsewhere, that it must be unified with the Infinite Root so that His mercy’s outpouring will not separate from this tenth world. And through the good deed of the lower ones with Israel, this unification is made, as said, and the power of the Lord grows, the left hand is included in the right, so that all fourteen bad times are included and sweetened with good.
Ki Teitzei: When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof etc. (Deut. 22:8). Now, it is stated in the Talmud of [Tractate] Gittin (7a): “He sent to Mar Ookva, ‘People are attacking...’ he drew lines and wrote to him, ‘Be still before the LORD and he will cast them down before you like so many corpses.’” The meaning is that when people sometimes afflict a certain person, it is because of the judgments against him Above; and [the judgments] clothe themselves in people Below to afflict him as is said about the verse, The LORD is on my side as my helper; I shall see through those who hate me (Ps. 118:7). The explanation: the fact that the judgments clothe themselves Below in people is helpful, since through this he can see what is also the case Above; which is to say, I shall see Above through those who hate me, meaning through the haters below. And the correction for this is to raise himself to the aspect of the world of Thought. For there [in the world of Thought] are no judgments, as is written, evil may not dwell with you (Ps. 5:5). And that means that through his remaining silent and accepting what comes to him, waiting quietly (Lam. 3:26) and elevating his thoughts as is written, Be still before the LORD etc. The explanation is that a person should elevate the silence, meaning the thought, to the LORD; and then they will fall like corpses, meaning the judgments will fall through the attachment of his thoughts to the LORD. And just as the roof is the essence of the house, similarly Thought is the essence of a person and shelters over him. For through Thought a person is preserved and knows how to settle himself as is known; and therefore Thought is called a “roof.”

Now, when a person builds a house it arouses the judgments, particularly outside the Land [of Israel] where it is full of all the emptiness of the world, as is known, and it constricts their borders. Therefore the Torah said, When you build a new house, you shall make, which is the idiom of correction, a parapet [ma’akeh] from the idiom of irritations [me’ikim]; the things that irritate you will be corrected through your attaching yourself Above to the place of Thought, which is your “roof” as we have said. And then, if you attach your Thought to the Blessed Creator, then when the one who falls will fall (Deut. 22:8) – as our Sages of Blessed Memory interpreted, he was destined to fall – for the judgments were destined to fall since the six days of Creation as is known; all of which is to say that the judgments will fall away from you, and understand this.
Vayeilech: 3. As I explained elsewhere, there are 600,000 letters in Torah.  Every Jew has a soul-root connected in one of the letters, each letter corresponding to the unique quality of his soul.  Accordingly, should he dicsonnect himself from Torah, God forbid, then one letter would be lacking from the Torah [thus making the entire Torah deficient].  That person would need to fix the difficiency in order to make it a whole Torah.

Another principle is every one of the 600,000 letter encompasses whole, from beginning to end, since each and every letter contains within it the entire Torah.  Therefore, if even one letter is missing from Torah, it is pasul [lacking the holiness needed for ritual use].  For this reason, every letter is considered to encompass the whole.
